what_was_done: In shell.py's _read_word, both the bare and the double-quoted $(( path now OR the arithmetic decision into subst instead of assigning it (subst = True only when the span is not plain arithmetic), so a '$(' or backtick earlier in the same word is no longer forgotten. _arithmetic_harmless replaces _arithmetic_nests_substitution: a $(( span is plain arithmetic only when it closes with '))' and its inner text holds only arithmetic characters, no '$(' and no backtick; anything else - '$((cmd) )', which sh and bash run as a command substitution, an unclosed span, one nesting '$(...)' - counts as a substitution. A '${...}' span holding a command substitution now sets subst too (the older gap: 'X=${y:-$(id)} ls' and 'echo > ${y:-$(id)}' are opaque), via the new _holds_substitution helper. _own_opacity no longer rescans argument text with the '$((' exclusion: opacity from substitutions rides each word's own subst flag, which _build_segment checks on the program, every assignment, every argument and every redirect target. Verified through the runner: an agent's 'vsdd survey $(id)$((1))' and 'vsdd survey $((id) )' produce no marker, no decision and no updatedInput (asserted in test_caller.py::test_decision_pairing). New tests: test_shell.py::test_substitution_beside_arithmetic_in_one_word_is_opaque (the six opaque cases of the finding plus 'echo > ${y:-$(id)}', and plain-arithmetic negatives including 'echo a$((1+2))b', '$(((1+2)))', '${y:-$((1+2))}') and test_caller.py's agent cases. Mutation checks: reverting the bare path to the assigning form fails both the shell test and test_decision_pairing; reverting the double-quoted path fails the shell test; dropping the '))'-close requirement fails both; disabling _holds_substitution fails the shell test. No C1-1 regression: 'vsdd survey --depth $((1+2))' keeps its marker (test_arithmetic_is_not_opaque_unless_it_runs_something passes).

emit.py now refuses to emit updatedInput without a permissionDecision: _deliver raises the new DecisionlessRewrite (a RuntimeError, exported in __all__) after logging rule.error for the rewriting rule, whenever a Rewrite outcome stands and the decision is None - today reachable when a rule returns Rewrite off PreToolUse (the old code silently dropped it), and the guard keeps HD7's pairing enforced against regression on PreToolUse. HD7 itself is unchanged, as the probe concludes: the platform applies a rewrite whether or not a decision travels with it, so the pairing cannot be dropped; the module docstring and the guard's comment say so, and rewrite/spec/topics/rule-model.md's passage on the decision now states it ('The pairing is never dropped...', with the round-4 Q4 probe named). New test: test_caller.py::test_decisionless_rewrite_never_leaves runs a rewriting rule on SessionStart and asserts the DecisionlessRewrite raise naming the rule and the decision. Mutation check: disabling the guard fails the test (no exception raised).

what_was_done: The parser already handles the leading-redirect form the finding asks for: _lex's digit-hug branch turns '2>' into a redirect operator, and _build_segment's redirect branch collects it into the redirect list whichever position it stands in, so '2>log cmd' parses program 'cmd' with redirects (('2>', 'log')), '>out cmd arg' parses program 'cmd', args ('arg',), redirects (('>', 'out')) - verified against the live parser before this round; the handling landed during the earlier S3R-hook-runner fix rounds and only lacked a pinning test. Added test_shell.py::test_leading_redirect_before_the_program asserting '2>log cmd' (program 'cmd', redirect ('2>', 'log')) and '>out cmd arg' (program 'cmd', args ('arg',), redirect ('>', 'out')), plus the trailing form unchanged. Mutation check: conditioning the redirect branch on at_program (leading redirects no longer collected) fails the test.

The spec example now shows what the runner prints: the Instead line carries the fix text as given, without the backticks and the trailing full stop, matching emit.block_lines (it prints f'Instead: {fix}') and the fix field of tests/unit/fixtures/schemas/event/valid_rule-block.json.
